plan.title: Liver treated vs control: descriptive DE, no replicates
plan.analytical_narrative: The data profile shows 1 treated vs 1 control liver sample (12000 genes x 2 samples, salmon-derived raw counts) with no biological replication. Per the grounded RNA-seq knowledge base (rule R-0003), a design with one sample per group provides no within-group variance from which to estimate dispersion, so no inferential p-value from DESeq2 or any count model has a valid statistical basis. The plan therefore runs: (1) sample-structure QC (library sizes, blind VST, PCA-adjacent distance check across only 2 samples, mainly for reporting rather than group discrimination), (2) low-count filtering and DESeq2 median-of-ratios normalization, (3) a strictly descriptive differential-expression step computing normalized counts and log2 fold changes (treated vs control) with no hypothesis test or FDR control, and (4) descriptive preranked GSEA using the log2FC as the ranking statistic against MSigDB Hallmark (human, 50 sets) and Reactome (human-filtered) gene sets available in the reference store, reported without set-level p-values as evidence, only as descriptive leading-edge signal. A final report step consolidates the findings, states every threshold and caveat, and gives the reproducibility record. No inferential DE test, shrinkage step, or multiple-testing correction is included, per the flagged design rule — these are the dropped steps.

steps.method: DESeq2 vst(blind) + PCA + sample distance heatmap
Keep genes with >=10 counts in at least 1 sample (smallest group size)
Descriptive log2 fold change only, no inferential test (no replication)
fgsea preranked GSEA on descriptive log2FC with MSigDB Hallmark, then Reactome
Descriptive DE + enrichment report with reproducibility record
